entities.summary: Pope Gregory V, born Bruno of Carinthia, was the bishop of Rome and ruler of the Papal States from 3 May 996 to his death. A member of the Salian dynasty, he was made pope by his cousin, Emperor Otto III. He played a crucial role in the Investiture Controversy, a power struggle between the Catholic Church and the Holy Roman Empire. Gregory V's papacy was marked by his efforts to assert papal authority and his attempts to resolve the conflict through diplomacy. He died on 28 February 999, following a mysterious illness that led to his death. His legacy as a leader of the Catholic Church during a pivotal moment in medieval history remains significant. The Investiture Controversy, which he helped to resolve, had far-reaching consequences for the relationship between the Church and the Empire, shaping the course of European history for centuries to come. Gregory V's papacy also saw the rise of the Ottonian dynasty, which would go on to shape the political landscape of Central Europe. The papacy of Gregory V stands as a testament to the enduring power of the Catholic Church in shaping the destiny of Europe.
